# A boolean attribute is present or absent, and setAttribute cannot say
# absent: `setAttribute("open", false)` renders `open="false"`, which leaves a
# <details> OPEN. Which props are boolean is what `element` declares, so both
# the initial-render path and the JS-built path read the declaration instead of
# each keeping a list — the two lists disagreed on hidden, readonly, selected
# and innerText, `open` was in neither, and `readonly` was written with the
# attribute's casing where the DOM property is readOnly.
#
# The prop the tag name binds to is read from the #[wildcard] mark's `into`
# argument for the same reason: it names the element and is never an attribute.

sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out dom.sngl

# Every boolean prop is a DOM property write, in the DOM's casing.
grep '__n0\.open = state\.shown;' out/index.html
grep '__n1\.readOnly = state\.locked;' out/index.html
! grep 'setAttribute\("open"' out/index.html
! grep 'setAttribute\("readonly"' out/index.html

# The same holds where the element is built by JS.
grep '__n2\.hidden = state\.shown;' out/index.html
! grep 'setAttribute\("hidden"' out/index.html

# The tag prop reaches no output on either path: it names the element.
grep '<my-widget role="main">' out/index.html
grep 'createElement\("li"\)' out/index.html
! grep 'tag="' out/index.html
! grep 'setAttribute\("tag"' out/index.html

-- dom.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main {
    var shown bool = false
    var locked bool = true
    var rows list<string> = ["a"]

    window {
        html.details(open = shown) {
            html.input(readonly = locked)
        }
        html.element(tag = "my-widget", role = "main")
        for r = rows {
            html.li(textContent = r, hidden = shown)
        }
    }
}
